problem: A self-consistent runtime report can assert an exact source mapping for substituted or unowned wheel code, an incorrect count or malformed archives; existing provider consumers do not independently recompute that mechanically available fact.
requirements: Keep report status, exact environment, artifact digest and raw evidence checks; never substitute recomputed byte parity for runtime execution or provider authority.

At the shared consuming boundary, validate both regular archives, extract only through the existing safe owner and recompute exact wheel/source correspondence from the supplied bytes before returning an accepted report.
Reject the build-manifest asset inventory and malformed provider artifact ID/digest before archive validation or runtime/source recomputation at the verifier consumer.
Compare the complete recomputed mapping with the declared mapping; booleans are not integer counts and undeclared mapping fields do not confer authority.
Reject substituted code, code lacking a source owner, false counts, ambiguous or unsafe archives and malformed source roots before verifier output or collection can advance.
Run no candidate interpreter, backend, import, installer or provider mutation to establish the byte-mapping fact. Retain owned temporary extraction cleanup.
Preserve unchanged genuine version-1.0 report payloads and public CLI grammar. This strengthens the existing fact check without a new schema, receipt, graph, registry or evaluator.
Keep immutable predecessor evidence unchanged; correct synthetic nonarchive fixtures instead of bypassing admission guards.
verification: Real matching and adversarial ZIP/tar fixtures with recomputed artifact digests; forbidden-subprocess control; affected runtime/provider/collector/toolchain tests, cause-specific disabled recomputation, mirrors and structural/semantic checks.
limits: Wheel-to-sdist correspondence is not authentication of the source commit or execution completeness.
Full lifecycle/profile/adopter conformance, composed deadlines, performance targets and independent release custody remain separately required.
